source_refs.note: vi) Noble Gases: a main subheading of 1.5 Families in the periodic table, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 6-6.

blocks.text: The noble gases are a group of unreactive elements present at the extreme right of the periodic table in Group 18. Examples include helium and argon. Due to their stable electron configuration (complete outermost shell), they are almost entirely unreactive under normal conditions and rarely form compounds with other elements. These elements are monoatomic in nature.

blocks.title: Keep in Mind
blocks.text: Although, noble gases are unreactive, however they have some compound. An example is compounds of xenon such as xenon hexafluoroplatinate (XePtF₆), the word inert gases was changed to noble gases.

blocks.prompt: a) Why are the elements in Groups 1 and 2 known as s-block elements?
blocks.explanation: The valence electrons of Groups 1 and 2 are in the s subshell: one (ns¹) in Group 1 and two (ns²) in Group 2. The block of an element is the subshell that receives its last electron, so these are s-block elements.

blocks.prompt: b) Name the elements in the chalcogen family. Give their two characteristics.
blocks.explanation: The chalcogens are the Group 16 elements: O, S, Se, Te, Po (and Lv). Two characteristics: (1) they have six electrons in the valence shell (ns² np⁴); (2) most ores of copper are their oxides or sulphides, which is why the name comes from the Greek chalkos (copper). Down the group the character changes from non-metal to metal.
